text:
maya: Heads-up: We saw ~18% drop in tokens/sec for EU-west during yesterday's lunch peak (11:30-12:15 UTC). P95 e2e latency jumped 180ms -> 420ms. Any correlation with concurrent reqs or network flaps? Posting quick snapshot:

maya: ```
euw1/p95_e2e: 180 -> 420 ms
tokens_per_sec: 250000 -> 205000
concurrent_reqs: 340 -> 710
net.tx_drops: +1200
cache_hit_rate: 96% -> 83%
```

alex: I see traces — grpc connect tails increased. Looks like spikes in tcp connect and small spikes in send queue. Could be queueing between LB and pods. @sam any infra churn?

sam: No sidecar config changes. We did push an autoscaler tweak to eu-infer-2 at ~11:10 (target CPU 60 -> 50%). Might've introduced scale jitter during the ramp.

maya: If autoscale churn happened, then cold starts + KV cache misses would reduce tokens/sec. Do we have exact cache hit rates around 11:30?

rachel: Cache hit dropped from 96% -> 83% in that window. Also saw prefix-cache eviction spikes: evict_count: 1200 between 11:05-11:20.

infra-bot: Alert: euw1-network-saturation detected at 11:12 UTC. eth0 tx drops +1200 since 11:00. Route flaps: 3.

alex: So multi-factor: autoscaler jitter -> cache evictions -> network saturation. We should treat this as correlated failures rather than single root cause. Quick mitigation: raise min_replicas for eu-infer-2 by +20% and add a soft per-host concurrent-request cap.

sam: Ran a small sim locally. If we cap per-host concurrent to 24, tokens/sec recovers but queueing shifts P95 slightly. Quick numbers: 

sam: ```
scenario A: min_replicas +20% => tokens/sec +12%, p95 -70ms
scenario B: cap_concurrent=24 => tokens/sec +9%, p95 +30ms
combined => tokens/sec +20%, p95 -40ms
```

rachel: Cost note: +20% min_replicas in EU = ~0.11 GPU-years/month => ~USD 6.5k/mo. Could offset by tightening batching and enabling int8/quant for idle models temporarily.

maya: Proposed immediate plan: 1) bump min_replicas today, 2) roll back the autoscaler tweak (target 60%), 3) relax prefix-cache TTL to reduce evictions, 4) canary per-host concurrent cap. Ops, can you schedule a short window?

carlos: On it. Scheduling 30-min maintenance at 16:00 UTC. Will run the min_replicas bump + autoscaler rollback first, monitor for 15m, then canary the cap. I'll post updates in this thread.

alex: Follow-ups for infra team: update throughput model to include a network-headroom term and an autoscaler-jitter penalty. We should run a traffic replay (last 6 months) to validate headroom thresholds.

maya: Agree. Sam/rachel — can you own the replay and updated tokens/sec headroom model? Need slides for next infra sync.

sam: I can own the replay. ETA: EOD tomorrow with initial artifacts.

rachel: I'll update the cost calc and the delta for enabling int8 on idle models. Ping me if you need numbers sooner.

maya: :thumbsup: thanks everyone. Ops — please tag #incidents when the maintenance starts and post results.

alex: One extra thing — add a short-term alert tuned to cache-eviction-rate x net.tx_drops correlation so we catch compound events earlier.

maya: Good call. Let's add that to the postmortem checklist after the replay completes.
